A family connection can start the journey. First, name the route.

Joining a partner, planning to marry, and joining a parent or child are different situations. The relationship, sponsor, and where each person is applying from can change which information matters.

Compare partner routes

A family relationship alone does not confirm a visa option.

Partner sponsorship is generally for a spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen. Other family categories have their own sponsors and requirements. Use the Department's current rules for the people and situation involved.

For partners, where you apply from matters.

These routes are distinct. Check the exact application and decision location rules before making plans.

01

Applying from outside Australia

The Partner (Provisional) visa subclass 309 is the first step toward the permanent Partner (Migrant) visa subclass 100. The temporary and permanent applications are made together. The applicant must be outside Australia when applying for this route.

Partner visas 309 and 100
Outside Australia at application
02

Applying from inside Australia

The Partner visa subclass 820 is the first step toward the permanent Partner visa subclass 801. The applicant must be in Australia when applying for this route. Check current visa conditions and onshore application rules first.

Partner visas 820 and 801
In Australia at application
03

Planning to marry your prospective spouse

The Prospective Marriage visa subclass 300 is a separate route for a person planning to marry their prospective spouse in Australia. You must be outside Australia when applying. Check the visa page for what follows the marriage.

Prospective Marriage visa 300
Outside Australia at application

For parents, children, and other relatives.

These are separate visa categories. The Department's finder can help you see which family category to investigate.

Child visasOptions depend on the child's circumstances and the parent's status.
Parent visasCheck sponsor and balance-of-family rules on the relevant visa page.
Other Family visasSome carer, aged dependent relative, and remaining relative visas are capped and queued.

Before you take the next step.

Build a short list of questions for the official visa page that fits your situation.

  1. 01

    Write down the relationship category and the sponsor's status.

  2. 02

    Confirm where the applicant must be when applying and when a decision is made.

  3. 03

    Check what the application asks for each person. Do not assume evidence from another couple's application will match yours.

  4. 04

    Review current processing information and plan for changes while an application is underway.

Organize your document questions

Open Path offers general information and lived experience, not migration advice or an assessment of eligibility. Visa rules, processing priorities, and individual circumstances matter. Always confirm details with the Department of Home Affairs.
